alerts.title: Abdominal pain: screen as suspected ADR
alerts.message: Guidelines require all healthcare workers to screen for suspected adverse drug reactions at each encounter using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs (mild or severe) should be recorded and reported. The patient reports abdominal pain today with no fever and normal appetite. TDF can cause gastrointestinal toxicity and renal-related abdominal symptoms. DTG is also associated with gastrointestinal side effects. However, non-drug causes such as dietary indiscretion, gastritis, or intercurrent infection should also be considered given the absence of fever.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen abdominal pain using the aDSM checklist; evaluate for drug and non-drug causes; record and report if ADR suspected.

alerts.title: Clinician plan lacks ADR evaluation
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for each encounter, all healthcare workers should screen for suspected ADRs using the Drug Safety Screening checklist. The clinician's plan today only restates the abdominal pain complaint without documenting any ADR screening, differential diagnosis, investigation, or management step. No orders or medicine changes were recorded. This represents a gap between the guideline requirement for systematic ADR screening and the documented plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Document ADR screening findings, assess abdominal pain etiology, and record any suspected ADR on the aDSM form for reporting.
